key_insight: This paper argues that human-AI interaction does not just change task performance; it can also reshape how people see themselves and how they connect with others. In other words, AI systems may influence identity, behavior, and social relationships over time.
problem_solved: It addresses the underexplored question of how repeated interactions with AI affect human self-perception and social networks, beyond immediate usability or accuracy metrics.
method: Conceptual/model-based analysis of how human-AI interaction can influence psychological and social processes.
Synthesizes evidence and theory from human-computer interaction, social psychology, and AI adoption.
Frames pathways by which AI may alter self-concept, trust, dependence, and social ties.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights that system design has social and psychological consequences, not just technical ones. It encourages building AI that supports healthy autonomy, trust, and human relationships.
visual_elements: A pathway diagram showing AI interaction -> self-perception changes -> social network changes
An icon-based comparison of benefits vs. risks of AI companionship and assistance
A layered network graphic illustrating shifting human relationships around an AI user
A timeline showing repeated AI exposure leading to gradual changes in behavior and identity
paper_title: Human–AI interactions reshape the self and our social networks
paper_authors: Andreia Sofia Teixeira, Sukhwinder Singh Shergill, Guy Laban
